name: @playliquid/engine-playcanvas
description: PlayLiquid GameOS PlayCanvas engine adapter (PL-021). An engine.playcanvas adapter implementing the neutral Adapter seam from @playliquid/engine-adapter-contract, registered into the Tool Fabric runtime (PL-019). PlayCanvas-specific behavior lives ONLY here (E4): a fixed web-first capability surface drawn from the Tool Fabric provider-neutral operation list (inspect project/scene/entity/component/asset, modify/import/export, run scene action/script, publish/play build target), each modeled as a typed, versioned command payload with total validation — typed kebab-case rejection codes, path-tagged, never any, never silent coercion. PlayCanvas-side execution stays behind the PlayCanvasBridgePort (pure interface): the adapter turns a validated neutral dispatch into a bridge-specific invocation (editor/web-publish pipeline envelope); the in-memory fake bridge is the test host. NO process spawning, no IO, no timers, no globals (E3) — the REAL PlayCanvas editor/publish invocation is the host's job (E11, deliberate deferral; R13: engines integrate through Tool Fabric only). Every outcome is stamped with an AdapterAuthority produced by the adapter/bridge; client-claimed outcomes are rejected by a total check (mirroring the contract's client-claim refusal pattern). Lifecycle transitions go exclusively through the contract's advanceLifecycle validator; dispatch in a non-active state is a typed refusal. Deterministic (E9): content-derived command ids, injected clock, seeded fakes, no Math.random, no wall clock. The typed PlayCanvasEngineBinding composes with the target-profiles engine-binding digest + build-contracts request vocabulary through a TYPED compatibility predicate (typed refusal, never a thrown exception) declaring the web-first target profiles it can serve (web, spark). Append-only evidence (E10): each dispatch/outcome pair is recorded as an immutable, content-addressed, digest-pinned exchange record, never edited. Cross-tenant isolation (R20): one tenant per adapter instance, typed tenancy rejections.
